# XeMFG component provenance

Imported from [dashdogy/MFG-Unlocker](https://github.com/dashdogy/MFG-Unlocker/tree/a4cf2c4ab632e84c72254932793bb9e64b33d76e/source/native), commit `a4cf2c4ab632e84c72254932793bb9e64b33d76e` (19 October 2026). The MIT copyright and permission notice are retained in `LICENSE.dashdogy.txt`; MinHook has its own notice.

R1.8 selectively updates `cuda/cuda_route.cpp` and `.h` from public MIT commit `29504cdd5d209a25e3b91e809a7e0d6f9db8cbdc` (v1.6.1): exact-length prefilter, bounded provider stack recognition through PSO recorders, and bounded refusal diagnostics. Our nonblocking `TrySnapshot` addition remains. `tests/xemfg_cuda` adapts that commit's recorder/wrapper and numerical tests. Its explicit `--shipped-programs` mode covers nine layer programs available in this build's verified inputs (five authored replacements and four original flow programs); it does not claim comparison against the eight unavailable original programs. The upstream strict full-fixture mode is retained.

The supplied v1.6.2.1022 ASI (`f34abd14975a5328ae3baf613f681b75d3075a4ff2a80da20cfefbaa0e9fab7b`) was inspected statically. Its executable code and new payloads were not loaded or imported. Public source refs were refreshed and still ended at the v1.6.1 commit above. The driver-metered queue-ahead path and Reflex output in R1.8 are independent adaptations, not a claim to reproduce every beta change. VSync, AL2 and dynamic XeMFG improvements from the announcement are not implemented by this change.

Reused components: decoded runtime layout witnesses, transactional count unlock, model catalog adaptation, shader decoder/program port, extra-output pacing and interval estimator, optional NVIDIA tensor-core route, SHA-256 helpers, native COM identity and NVAPI ownership validation. Include paths and the small logging/COM host adapters were adapted for this project. `image_slots.h` contains only the two image-range checks consumed by `overlay_native.h`. Our `port_support.h` supplies the logging and common declarations; it does not integrate the original renderer.

The standalone DLSS implementation, overlay renderer, preset controls, motion-vector repair, HUD matching, scene-change override and Intel-architecture unlock were **not** imported. Our `backend.cpp` handles model startup admission and real context lifecycle. The legacy ASI build relies on OptiScaler for transport. The native ReShade build instead uses our independent `native_bridge`, `native_streamline` and `native_swapchain` implementations; it does not require OptiScaler. R1.2 adds our own `native_controls` and owner-thread `native_window` controller. The small additions to imported `sdk_pacing` expose a context-scoped read-only status and queue overlay requests for a batch boundary; they do not transplant OptiScaler's renderer or latency policies.

`runtime_layout.generated.h` is the upstream source-level instruction-profile metadata, not a shader/model payload. The three local NVIDIA-generated headers remain exactly the official 1.4.5 inputs. No DR1, MR1, CA1, TGL or LMR kernel change is in this branch.

Intel-derived DXIL programs are separate local build inputs and retain Intel's terms (`XEFG-PROGRAMS-NOTICE.txt`). The 54-program manifest is pinned by upstream SHA-256. The seven authored shader outputs and the CUDA fatbin have their upstream generator hashes. For this local build they are statically read from the user's supplied 1.6.0.1010 ASI, after checking its complete SHA-256; its executable code is not loaded. They are not checked into this repository. The source HLSL/CUDA and pinned compiler recipes are included, but compiling those recipes was not a validation performed by this build. Intel runtime DLLs and model weights are supplied by the user's existing installation.

OptiScaler source was inspected as an API/ownership reference; no GPL OptiScaler implementation is copied here. The official Intel SDK headers are externally supplied (their MIT notice is retained with the packaged notices).

R1.10 compares the public OptiScaler checkout at `c2e44a8bc911010d7ed3e4fa63843185fbb55d03` only for architecture and API coverage. Historical Streamline markers, guarded native queue/factory transport, context-lifecycle serialization and optional CPU/GPU stall tracing are independent changes to this project's bridge. The small `RuntimeCall` additions in `sdk_pacing.cpp` and `cuda_route.cpp` observe existing calls only in the native addon build; they import no new upstream pacing algorithm and remove no SDK synchronization.

R1.11's `native_factory` and `native_continuity` are independently authored MIT adapters using public DXGI COM, `ResizeBuffers1` and window-generation properties. They retain/release only references owned by this bridge. Game depth defaults are backed by local Streamline constant receipts. No OptiScaler implementation, shader/model payload or new upstream pacing algorithm is imported by these changes.

Plan 5.3 vendors four public FidelityFX API headers (`ffx_api/ffx_api.h`, `ffx_api_types.h`, `ffx_framegeneration.h`, `dx12/ffx_api_dx12.h`) unchanged from [GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK) tag `v1.1.4`, with AMD's MIT notice in `ffx_api/LICENSE.txt`. Only the declarations are used: the adapter in `native_ffx.cpp` is our own and loads no FidelityFX code; the game's FidelityFX loader is hooked at runtime.

1.7 (plan F) vendors the xvk D3D12-on-Vulkan layer unchanged from [dashdogy/MFG-Unlocker](https://github.com/dashdogy/MFG-Unlocker/tree/v1.7.0/source/native/xess/vulkan) tag `v1.7.0` (commit `b97deee`, MIT, notice in `LICENSE.dashdogy.txt`): `xvk.h`, `xvk_internal.h`, `xvk_embedded.h`, `xvk_output_frame.h` and the eight `xvk_*.cpp` files in `vendor/xvk`. Only `single_module.h` is ours: the one logging entry point xvk uses, implemented on the XeMFG log. The 83 SPIR-V programs xvk runs are translations of Intel's XeFG DXIL and keep Intel's terms: `tools/extract_xvk_programs.py` reads them, without loading any code, from the user's own copy of the v1.7.0 release DLL (its SHA-256 is checked), and `tools/generate_xvk_programs.py` embeds them at build time. Neither the SPIR-V nor the Khronos `Vulkan-Headers` (`vulkan-sdk-1.4.350.1`, Apache-2.0/MIT) are committed; the `xemfg_xvk` target is built only when both are present locally.

1.7 (plan J) brings the engine files that changed upstream up to dashdogy's v1.7.0 (`b97deee`) by a three-way merge against the original import base (`a4cf2c4`): `sdk_pacing.cpp/.h`, `sdk_pacing_dlssg.h`, `cuda/cuda_route.cpp/.h`, `host_unlock.cpp/.h` and `port/shader_port.h`, with this project's local changes (runtime traces, flip-metering/queue-ahead/SDK-deadline controls and their status snapshot) kept. New upstream files: `sdk_pacing_meter.h` (the flip queue), `cadence_stats.h` and `adapter_vendor_kmt.h`, unchanged. `optiscaler_host.h` is ours: the single constant the pacing component reads, since this build never runs under OptiScaler. `xess_mod.h` stays this project's adapter (upstream's declares its whole host module, which this build replaces). `native_xvk_stub.cpp` supplies the two xvk output-frame hooks the pacing component calls until the Vulkan host exists. The flip queue is configured by `backend.cpp` and stays off by default, as upstream's own standalone D3D12 host does.

1.7 (plan F, Vulkan host) vendors the host that runs xvk on a game's own VkDevice from the same tag (`b97deee`, MIT): `xvkhost/vk_host.cpp`, `vk_host.h` and `mfg_xefg_vk.h` from `source/native/xess/vulkan`, and from `source/native/xess` the headers it includes, unchanged: `standalone_policy.h`, `runtime_search.h`, `xemfg_window.h`, `xemfg_dynamic.h`, `xefg_dynamic_count.h`, `xefg_dynamic_cap.h`. `xvkhost/xess/xess_mod.h` is ours (it forwards to this project's adapter, which now declares the Vulkan host's route calls; `backend.cpp` implements them on the validated pair). The input-copy shader (`vk_input_copy.comp`, upstream MIT GLSL) is used as its three pinned SPIR-V variants, read with their upstream SHA-256 from the same release DLL by `tools/extract_xvk_programs.py`; nothing is committed. Upstream's `overlay_vulkan.cpp` (its vulkan-1 resolver hooks) and its NGX route are **not** imported: `native_vulkan.cpp` is this project's own adapter (hooks on vulkan-1's exports, installed from ReShade's `create_device` for Vulkan, and on `_nvngx.dll`'s `NVSDK_NGX_VULKAN_*` exports).

Local changes to the vendored Vulkan files are marked `MFGAdaUnlock 1.7` in place, each found in the field on Indiana Jones and the Great Circle (Streamline, DLSS Ray Reconstruction, ReShade as a Vulkan layer):
- `vk_host.cpp`: standalone chains accept `VK_KHR_present_id`, `VK_KHR_present_wait`, `VK_NV_low_latency2` and `VK_EXT_full_screen_exclusive`, whose commands on the host's chain `native_vulkan.cpp` answers (upstream accepts them only under OptiScaler).
- `vk_host.cpp`: the DLSS input copy runs at the frame's present on the host's own command buffer, submitted with the bridge after the game's semaphores (`DeferredCopy`). Recorded in DLSS's command buffer, its compute pipeline, push descriptors and constants replaced the game's compute state, which this game does not bind again after DLSS: the GPU hung. Upstream's in-place recording stays available (`[XeFG] VulkanInputCopy=6`).
- `vk_host.cpp`: the copy samples single-aspect views the addon creates per input image (the game's depth view spans depth and stencil while NGX is told it is a color view).
- `vk_host.cpp`, `xvk.h`, `xvk_internal.h`, `xvk_device.cpp`, `xvk_dxgi.cpp`: NVIDIA's present metering (`VK_NV_present_metering`, the Vulkan form of the NVAPI flip metering the D3D12 path uses) is requested on the device where the driver offers it, and each batch's first present carries `VkSetPresentConfigNV` with the frames XeFG presents per base frame (`[XeFG] VulkanPresentMetering`, on by default; not under V-Sync).
- `xvk_dxgi.cpp`: 1.7.1, alt-tab mitigation. While the present thread remakes a swap chain, its staging slot is released and `Present1` drops its frame instead of entering the driver, and no chain is made for a window with a 0x0 extent. It makes the driver hang in `vkCreateSwapchainKHR` rarer; it does not remove it.
- `vk_host.cpp`: with the addon's own views, a depth+stencil depth view is accepted (Red Dead Redemption 2 passes its D32S8 depth that way; upstream refused every input of that game).
- `vk_host.cpp`: standalone chains that name a full-screen-exclusive mode are eligible; the addon creates every chain of the game with the mode disallowed (named explicitly when the game enabled the extension without naming one: the driver otherwise kept the display on the game's retired chain in RDR2's fullscreen mode) and answers the mode commands. Mailbox chains are created immediate.
- `vk_host.cpp`: field isolation switches `[XeFG] VulkanInputCopy` and `VulkanGenerate` (diagnostics only).
`native_xvk_stub.cpp` is now compiled only into builds without the Vulkan host.
